summary: Megatron-LM trains transformer language models of up to 8.3 billion parameters by splitting the GEMMs of each transformer layer across up to 8 GPUs by hand: the first MLP and the K/Q/V GEMMs column-wise, the following GEMMs row-wise, with two programmer-inserted conjugate autograd operators that perform all-reduces. It needs no compiler, combines with 64-way data parallelism, and reaches 74 percent weak-scaling efficiency on 512 V100 GPUs.
why_read: It is the hand-written intra-layer tensor-parallel scheme that automatic sharding compilers reproduce and benchmark against.
main_contribution: A column-then-row GEMM partitioning of transformer blocks that needs only two all-reduces per layer in each direction, implemented by inserting two autograd operators into existing PyTorch code, plus fusing parallel logits with the loss to avoid an all-gather.
main_limitation: Partitioning is derived manually for transformer blocks only; model-parallel groups are confined to one server, so models beyond about 16B parameters need inter-layer and inter-node parallelism the paper leaves to future work; strong scaling shows diminishing returns beyond 2 GPUs.
evaluation_method: Weak and strong scaling of GPT-2 configurations on up to 32 DGX-2H servers (512 V100 GPUs) against a single-GPU 1.2B baseline, plus downstream accuracy studies
benchmarks: BERT 336M/1.3B/3.9B on MNLI, QQP, SQuAD 1.1/2.0, RACE
states_relationship_to: Chen, Yang, Cheng 2018, model parallelism on multi-GPU platform
notes: Paper uses author-year citations, so no reference numbers exist. ir_representation is 'none' because the text states no compiler is involved (Sec. 3). compiler_runtime_boundary and compiler_architecture left empty for the same reason.
